{{Quote|Today, I'm excited to share with you that Jon and Dave are concurrently developing two new spinoff series exclusively for Disney+: one, ''The Rangers of the New Republic'', and the other featuring fan-favorite Ahsoka Tano.|Lucasfilm President Kathleen Kennedy announces ''Rangers of the New Republic'' during Disney Investor Day 2020|<ref name="Investor2020">{{DisneyCompany|url=disney-investor-day-2020|text=Disney Investor Day 2020}}</ref>}}
'''''Rangers of the New Republic''''' was a planned live-action television series. It was announced on [[December 10]], [[2020]], and would have been executive produced by [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Jon Favreau]] and starred [[Gina Carano]] as the character [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]]. As of [[November]] [[2021]], [[Lucasfilm]] President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] confirmed that the series was canceled, saying that no scripts had been written and that concepts would be absorbed into future episodes of ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''.

==Official description==
''Set within the timeline of ''The Mandalorian'', this new live-action series from executive producers Jon Favreau and Dave Filoni will intersect with future stories and culminate into a climactic story event.''<ref name="Announcement" />

==Development==
{{Quote|Set within the timeline of ''The Mandalorian'', these interconnected shows, along with future stories, will excite new audiences, embrace our most passionate fans, and will culminate in a climactic story event.|Lucasfilm President Kathleen Kennedy announces ''Rangers of the New Republic'' during Disney Investor Day 2020|<ref name="Investor2020" />}}
[[File:Kathleen_Kennedy_Rangers_Announce.png|thumb|250px|Kathleen Kennedy announces ''Rangers of the New Republic'' and ''Ahsoka'' at Disney Investor Day 2020.]]
In [[February]] of [[2020]], [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] CEO [[Bob Iger (chief executive officer)|Bob Iger]] hinted in an earnings call that spinoff series featuring characters from ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' were in development.<ref name="The HR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/disneys-bob-iger-teases-mandalorian-falcon-winter-soldier-wandavision-dates-1276326|text=Disney's Bob Iger Considering 'Mandalorian' Spinoff Shows|author=Couch, Aaron|date=2020-02-04|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20230206194040}}</ref> [[Lucasfilm]] President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] announced that ''Rangers of the New Republic'' and ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]'' were among those series during a Disney Investor Day presentation on [[December 10]] of that year. She stated that they and "future stories" would be take place in ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} timeline<ref name="Investor2020" />—which is set around [[9 ABY]]<ref name="Rangers of the New Republic date" />—and "culminate in a climactic story event."<ref name="Investor2020" />

On [[February 10]], [[2021]], [[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']] reported that actress [[Gina Carano]]<ref name="The Hollywood Reporter Gina">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/the-mandalorian-star-gina-carano-fired-amid-social-media-controversy-4131168|text='The Mandalorian' Star Gina Carano Fired Amid Social Media Controversy|author=Parker, Ryan; Couch, Aaron|date=2021-02-10|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20231220140009}}</ref>—who had played [[Marshal]] of the [[New Republic]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] in ''The Mandalorian''<ref name="Chapter 14">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}}</ref>—was originally slated to be revealed as the star of a spinoff series during the 2020 Disney Investor Day presentation. On the same day, Lucasfilm denounced "abhorrent" social media posts by Carano in a public statement and confirmed that Carano was not currently employed by the company, nor would she be employed in any future projects.<ref name="The Hollywood Reporter Gina" /> On [[May 20]], in an interview with [[Dave Filoni]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] reported that the series was no longer in active development.<ref name="Variety">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/star-wars-the-mandalorian-dave-filoni-lucasfilm-creative-director-1234978130|text='The Mandalorian' EP Dave Filoni's 'New' Job at Lucasfilm Isn't Actually New, but Fans on Twitter Got Excited Anyway|author=Vary, Adam B.|date=2021-05-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20210521073715}}</ref> In an interview with Kathleen Kennedy in the [[January]] [[2022]] issue of [[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']], it was confirmed that ''Rangers'' had indeed been intended to star Carano as Cara Dune and that the series was canceled. Kennedy added that scripts were never written for the series, and concepts and ideas from it would be incorporated into future episodes of ''The Mandalorian''.<ref name="Empire" />

On [[February 6]], [[2024]], Carano filed a lawsuit for discrimination and wrongful termination against Disney and Lucasfilm, seeking to be recast in ''Star Wars'' and receive compensation for ''Rangers of the New Republic''{{'s}} cancelation.<ref name="Lawsuit">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/gina-carano-sues-disney-mandalorian-firing-lawsuit-elon-musk-1235817466|text=Gina Carano Sues Disney Over 'Mandalorian' Firing in Lawsuit Funded by Elon Musk|author=Winston Cho|date=2023-02-06|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20240206212957}}</ref> On [[August 7]], [[2025]], Disney, Lucasfilm, and Carano announced that they had reached a settlement over the lawsuit.<ref name="Settlement 2025">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/gina-carano-disney-settle-mandalorian-firing-1236481982|text=Gina Carano, Disney Settle Legal Dispute Over 'Mandalorian' Firing|author=[https://variety.com/author/katcy-stephan Katcy Stephan]|date=2025-08-07|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20250808004519}}</ref>
